description: One curious mind, endless possibilities. Exploring ideas, discovering new things and taking on challenges beyond Earth.
summary:
TERA-SPACE explores how selected environments on Earth can serve as terrestrial analogs for understanding the geological features and surface conditions of Mars. The project focuses on the Atacama Desert in Chile and Icelandic volcanic terrain, comparing their documented characteristics with the Syrtis Major region of Mars.

The project develops a comparative framework to identify geological features, environmental characteristics and terrain conditions that may be relevant to Martian exploration. It addresses the challenge by examining how different Earth environments can provide useful insights into planetary surface studies, rather than relying solely on visual similarities.

This research is important because terrestrial analogs provide accessible environments for studying geological processes and supporting the preparation of future robotic exploration missions. By highlighting both their potential and limitations, TERA-SPACE aims to contribute to a better understanding of how Earth-based research can support future exploration of Mars.
details:
TERA-SPACE is a research-based project that evaluates the potential of selected terrestrial environments as analogs for Martian geological studies. It uses information from NASA, USGS and scientific publications to examine the Atacama Desert, Icelandic volcanic terrain and Syrtis Major on Mars.

The project uses a self-contained MATLAB programme to organise geological evidence, display terrain imagery and compare the spatial resolutions of planetary datasets. It was developed using MATLAB and published planetary data references without requiring additional hardware or external software tools.

Its main benefit is providing a simple way to understand how different Earth environments can contribute to Mars-related research. The project combines geological information, planetary observations and engineering considerations in one visual framework. Factors considered include geological characteristics, available terrain information, spatial resolution and the limitations of using Earth environments to represent Martian conditions. Its intended impact is to support preliminary analog-site research and encourage further investigation for future robotic exploration.
